title: Bragulla et al. 2026 — pristine ZrN-GDE at open-circuit voltage (in situ online IC)
description: In situ background measurement: a pristine ZrN gas-diffusion electrode (Nafion ionomer in the catalyst layer) mounted in the electrochemical cell with 0.2 M H2SO4 and no electrochemistry (OCV). Every nmol of ammonium measured here is, by construction, not electrochemical N2 reduction. The case shows why an observation that exceeds the separately quantified material contamination does NOT establish nitrogen reduction: the separately measured components (24 h aging tests, Table 1) do not account for the in-cell value, and the authors attribute the difference to ammonium released from the Nafion ionomer of the GDE.

evidence.quote: the NH4+ and Ca2+ concentration quickly increase, reaching asymptotic time‐weighted average values of 85.2 (2.76 µg) and 77.6 µg L−1, respectively.
evidence.note: Time-weighted average; no uncertainty interval reported, so a point value is used. Total run time of Fig. 8 not stated in the main text. 2.76 µg / 85.2 µg/L implies ≈32 mL, consistent with the 32 mL in SI Figs S2/S3 (§3.6 says 'about 35 mL').

evidence.quote: The nitrogen supply was of 5.0 quality, which contained an ammonia contamination of only 80 ppbmol (see Supoorting Information).
evidence.note: Measured for the unpurified house supply by gas washing. NOx was not measured. Whether gas flowed through the cell during the OCV measurement is not stated in the main text.

evidence.quote: The EC setup was identical to an actual electrochemical measurement except for a reference electrode or electrical connections, that is, at open‐circuit voltage (OCV).
evidence.note: Gas flow during this measurement: not stated → gas source left unbounded.

evidence.quote: The total amount of NH4+ liberated from the GDE accounting for the GDL is 1.55 µg. This equals 1.03 µg cm−2 (1.51 cm2 sample) or 0.66 pmol cm−2 s−1 per 24 h.

assumptions: Observed amount is the reported time-weighted average (2.76 µg NH4+); no measurement interval is reported.
No electrochemical potential was applied, so the observed ammonium is a background by experimental design.
